name: sol_defi_lending_11
description: Liquidation reward calculation can silently shortchange liquidators without revert or slippage protection
question: The source file in `source` implements a liquidation function that computes and transfers a collateral/reward amount to the liquidator, but that amount can be silently reduced below what the liquidator expected (e.g., via capping to available balance, rounding down, or a price/ratio that changes mid-transaction) without reverting and without any liquidator-specified minimum-amount or slippage check, so the liquidator can receive less than anticipated; this excludes cases where the liquidator supplies a minCollateralOut/minReward parameter that reverts on underpayment, or where the reduced payout is an intentional, fixed, and clearly documented admin-configured liquidation bonus.
criteria: liquidate() computes seizeAmount = debtToCover * price / collateralPrice then pays min(seizeAmount, availableCollateral) to the liquidator without reverting or reducing debtToCover proportionally
liquidation reward is computed via integer division that rounds down the collateral amount sent to the liquidator with no check against an expected minimum
liquidate() has no minCollateralOut or minReward parameter, so price movement between submission and execution can silently lower the payout with no revert
multiple liquidators can partially liquidate the same position such that a later liquidator's seized collateral is reduced by earlier calls without any notification or revert
